problem: Team Kanban_IBM Z Datathon 2026 Project: IntentGate Z. AI agents are being given real tools: dispatching ambulances, reserving ICU beds, raising purchase orders. Authentication proves WHO an agent is and WHICH tools it may call, but not whether the specific action it is about to take is what the human actually asked for. A routing agent can read a poisoned hospital-status feed and redirect a critical patient while fully authenticated; a procurement agent can turn a $50,000 restock into a $200,000 order; a coordination agent can drift beyond its task. On the public InjecAgent benchmark (Zhan et al., 2024), ReAct-prompted GPT-4 agents followed indirect prompt injections 24% of the time, nearly doubling under an enhanced attack. In emergency operations, healthcare and finance an unintended action can cost lives or money. The missing control is a real-time check, at the moment of action and before execution, that an agent's proposal still matches the human's intent, with evidence a person can audit.
solution: IntentGate Z is a gateway between autonomous agents and sensitive tools. The operator registers a signed, versioned, immutable intent (allowed operations, targets, budget, ETA limit, expiry). Every agent tool call carries parameter-level provenance (trusted operator / internal system / untrusted feed). The gateway (Python, FastAPI, Pydantic) runs identity and tool-capability checks; hard policy (scope, budget and escalation ceiling, capacity, route integrity, trust boundary, patient-data egress, replay); 43 contextual features; two text models (untrusted-feed instructions, agent-rationale deference); and an ML risk model. Hard rules always win; the model can only escalate, and an ML-driven BLOCK needs structural corroboration. ALLOW executes; CHALLENGE needs a single-use, 120-second supervisor grant bound to the action fingerprint and re-checked before execution; BLOCK prevents. Every step goes to a SHA-256 hash-chained audit log. A React/Three.js 3D command center renders only server decisions.
ibm_z: Everything runs on our IBM LinuxONE Community Cloud VM (s390x, machine type 9175 = IBM z17, z/VM 7.3, CPU flag nnpa). The gateway runs in Docker, built FROM IBM's s390x AI/ML image, behind Caddy HTTPS on the same VM; Jupyter only via SSH tunnel. We generated the data and trained and evaluated every model on LinuxONE (scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch). The live risk model is a PyTorch MLP served on the Telum on-chip AI accelerator through IBM torch_nnpa; the API verifies at start-up that its parameters live on the NNPA and match CPU outputs (max diff 0.002). Measured on the VM: NNPA up to 2.15x faster than CPU at batch 1024; gateway decision p50 0.41 ms, about 1,400 decisions/s in-process; 352-396 requests/s over HTTP (1-16 concurrent) with 0 errors. We ran both IBM labs (Churn multi-model; Loan Approval with Granite) and reuse the image's Granite model via llama.cpp for optional explanations. IBM Z fits because the security decision sits next to the systems it protects, with on-chip AI and enterprise isolation.
value: Beneficiaries: emergency dispatchers and hospital command centers adopting AI agents, public emergency agencies, healthcare IT and security teams, and IBM Z customers (banks, insurers, governments) that want agents to act on core systems safely. Outcome: agents keep their speed for routine work while unintended or manipulated actions are stopped before they execute, and exceptional ones reach the right human with evidence. Across five independently generated datasets evaluated on LinuxONE, the hybrid gateway let 0.8% of unsafe actions through, versus 5.3% for hard rules alone, 3.8% for rules plus heuristics and 3.4% for ML alone, while wrongly blocking 0% of legitimate actions (ML alone blocked 6.9%). It stopped 94% of injections that steer an agent to a permitted-but-wrong hospital, where rules alone let half through. Value: a drop-in, auditable checkpoint (policy-as-code plus on-chip ML) that turns 'authorized' into 'authorized AND intended'. All data is synthetic; this is an educational proof of concept.
